title: Renal Comprehensive Set 1: Glomerular Filtration (Short Answer)

questions.prompt: What are the three main regions of the kidney when viewed in a sagittal section?
questions.modelAnswer: Cortex, medulla (outer and inner), and papilla.

questions.prompt: Contrast the location of the glomeruli and the length of the loops of Henle in superficial cortical nephrons versus juxtamedullary nephrons.
questions.modelAnswer: Superficial: Glomeruli in outer cortex, short loops. Juxtamedullary: Glomeruli near corticomedullary border, long loops descending into the inner medulla.

questions.prompt: Which type of nephron is essential for the concentration of urine, and what is its specialized vascular component called?
questions.modelAnswer: Juxtamedullary nephrons; vasa recta.

questions.prompt: Identify the three layers of the glomerular capillary wall that constitute the filtration barrier.
questions.modelAnswer: Endothelium (pores), basement membrane, and epithelium (podocytes).

questions.prompt: Why are negatively charged macromolecules, such as plasma proteins, filtered less readily than neutral molecules of the same size?
questions.modelAnswer: The filtration barrier contains fixed negative charges (glycoproteins) that repel negatively charged solutes.

questions.prompt: Which specialized epithelial cells form the "filtration slits" in the glomerular barrier?
questions.modelAnswer: Podocytes.

questions.prompt: Write the Starling equation as it specifically applies to the Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR).
questions.modelAnswer: GFR=Kf[(PGC-PBS)-πGC ].

questions.prompt: Why is the oncotic pressure in Bowman's space (π_(BS)) normally considered to be zero?
questions.modelAnswer: Because the filtration of protein is negligible.

questions.prompt: Contrast the behavior of hydrostatic pressure (P_(GC)) along the length of a glomerular capillary with that of a systemic capillary.
questions.modelAnswer: P_(GC)  remains constant along the entire length of the glomerular capillary, whereas systemic capillary hydrostatic pressure falls.

questions.prompt: What causes the oncotic pressure in the glomerular capillary (π_(GC)) to increase along its length?
questions.modelAnswer: As fluid is filtered out, protein is left behind and becomes more concentrated.

questions.prompt: Define "filtration equilibrium" in the context of glomerular Starling forces.
questions.modelAnswer: The point where the net ultrafiltration pressure becomes zero because π_(GC)  has risen to equal the net hydrostatic pressure.

questions.prompt: How is the filtration fraction calculated, and what is its approximate normal value?
questions.modelAnswer: FF=GFR/RPF; approximately 0.20 (or 20%).

questions.prompt: What is the effect of an increased filtration fraction on the oncotic pressure of the peritubular capillaries?
questions.modelAnswer: It increases the protein concentration and oncotic pressure (πc ) of the peritubular capillary blood.

questions.prompt: Explain the "Myogenic Hypothesis" of renal autoregulation in response to an increase in renal arterial pressure.
questions.modelAnswer: Increased pressure stretches afferent arterioles, causing them to contract (via stretch-activated Ca^(2+)  channels), increasing resistance to maintain constant flow.

questions.prompt: Which region of the distal tubule senses changes in load to provide "Tubuloglomerular Feedback"?
questions.modelAnswer: Macula densa.

questions.prompt: In the tubuloglomerular feedback mechanism, what is the effector response when the macula densa senses an increased delivered load of NaCl?
questions.modelAnswer: It releases a vasoactive substance (e.g., adenosine) to constrict the afferent arteriole, reducing GFR back to normal.

questions.prompt: Why does a high-protein diet lead to an increase in GFR?
questions.modelAnswer: It increases NaCl reabsorption in the proximal tubule, decreasing delivery to the macula densa, which triggers the tubuloglomerular feedback to increase GFR.

questions.prompt: How does the sympathetic nervous system affect renal blood flow (RBF) and GFR, and which receptor is primarily involved?
questions.modelAnswer: It constricts afferent arterioles more than efferent, decreasing both RBF and GFR; α1  receptors.

questions.prompt: Describe the preferential action of low levels of Angiotensin II on the renal arterioles and its subsequent effect on GFR.
questions.modelAnswer: It preferentially constricts efferent arterioles, which increases PGC  and thereby "protects" or increases GFR despite a decrease in RPF.

questions.prompt: What are the simultaneous effects of Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (ANP) on the afferent and efferent arterioles?
questions.modelAnswer: Dilation of afferent arterioles and constriction of efferent arterioles (both of which increase GFR).

questions.prompt: Which paracrine substances are produced locally to attenuate the vasoconstrictor effects of the sympathetic nervous system and Angiotensin II?
questions.modelAnswer: Prostaglandins (PGE2and PGI2 ).

questions.prompt: How do Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs) potentially lead to renal failure during a hemorrhage?
questions.modelAnswer: They inhibit prostaglandin synthesis, removing the protective vasodilatory effect that normally prevents excessive renal ischemia.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of a low-dosage infusion of dopamine on renal arterioles?
questions.modelAnswer: It dilates renal arterioles and increases RBF.

questions.prompt: How does a ureteral stone (calculus) decrease GFR in terms of Starling forces?
questions.modelAnswer: It increases the hydrostatic pressure in Bowman's space (PBS ), which opposes filtration.

questions.prompt: What is the role of mesangial cells in determining the filtration coefficient (Kf )?
questions.modelAnswer: Contraction of mesangial cells reduces the total surface area available for filtration, thus decreasing Kf  and GFR.

questions.prompt: If the afferent arteriole is dilated and no other changes occur, what happens to RPF and GFR?
questions.modelAnswer: Both RPF and GFR increase.

questions.prompt: Why does an increase in plasma protein concentration decrease GFR?
questions.modelAnswer: It increases the oncotic pressure in the glomerular capillary (π_(GC)), which opposes filtration.
